title: Rift MCP surface
description: JSON values accepted and returned by the Rift MCP server. Each definition carries its Protobuf identity.

rift:entryPoints.description: Requests do not open connection-scoped sessions. Each call names a projection or the workspace tree and carries every witnessed address it uses. A cursor names a process-local captured result; a projection retains its changes and recorded read dependencies across calls. The typed result rides `structuredContent` against the tool's declared output schema, mirrored as one canonical-JSON `text` block, and a refusal is such a result — never `isError`. `ErrorData` travels as the JSON-RPC error object's `data` with code -32000. The server serializes change application per targeted tree; a cancelled queued change is dropped, and a cancelled running change completes or rolls back whole. Each resource entry maps one URI family to the types that carry it.

server.lock.description:
The rendezvous record at `.rift/server.json`, written by the server that owns the
    workspace and read by every process that wants to reach it. Atomic creation of the file
    is the election: the process that creates it starts the server, and everyone else
    connects to the endpoint it names. The file is readable by its owner alone, so holding
    the token is what authorizes a connection — localhost TCP carries no peer identity the
    server could check instead.

get_symbol.description: Gets project, dependency, or standard-library declarations by name. Each hit includes declaration source when the provider can read it; `include_body: false` omits it, and `include_history` adds project version-control history. Use `search` for lexical, filtered, or relationship discovery.

search.description: Searches symbols, nodes, and files by lexical `query`, provider `filter`, or bounded relationship `traversal`. `scope` selects project, dependency, or all sources. Use `traversal` for callers, callees, tests, edit ripple, or review context; use `get_symbol` when the declaration name is known.

nodes.description: Lists syntax nodes covering one byte position and returns witnessed addresses for `replace_node`. Use it when the target is smaller than a declaration.

replace_symbol.description: Replaces one declaration addressed by symbol, with no caller-supplied offsets. The symbol must resolve to project source; dependency, standard-library, external, and synthetic declarations refuse as unsupported. Use `replace_node` for a smaller syntax region or `patch` for scattered hunks.

insert_symbol.description: Inserts a new declaration immediately before or after an existing one. The parser decides the exact bytes, so the insertion cannot land inside a neighboring declaration.

replace_node.description: Replaces one syntax node, addressed by a witnessed identity a `nodes` listing returned. A stale listing refuses instead of splicing into moved bytes.

patch.description: Applies every hunk of one unified diff atomically. Use it for scattered hunks, file creation, or changes no symbol or node address expresses.

projection_create.description: Creates a pinned workspace snapshot. Changes targeting its id write the projection directory until `publish` copies them into the workspace.

projection_list.description: Lists projections and the state of each.

projection_remove.description: Removes one projection and deletes its directory, unpublished changes included.

projection_restore.description: Restores a projection's changed paths from the workspace and drops the changes that touched them.

publish.description: Reconciles direct filesystem writes, then publishes a projection's changeset into the workspace. A changed write path, an unaccepted confirmation, or a changed read dependency refuses the whole publication.

execute.description: Evaluates code in the targeted tree's execution copy, where installed dependencies persist between calls. The server does not synchronize copy writes back, but the runtime retains the server's OS permissions outside that directory.

workspace.description: Reports the providers serving each language, limits, and hooks.

projection.description: Returns the filesystem path and state of one projection, for tools that can only work through a directory.

changes.description: Returns one changeset — the workspace journal, or a projection's — each change with its edits, effects, advisories, and the confirmations publication will check.

fs.description: Returns one page of a directory's entries — subdirectories and files — or a bounded file-content range from the workspace tree.

rift:axes.description: Each axis owns a set of definitions. `identifiedBy` supplies its roots, then the group closes over references without taking a definition already assigned to another axis. `holds` assigns explicit definitions and `residualOf` assigns the unclaimed definitions from one schema document.

Advisory.description:
One concern a provider or hook attached to an applied change, injected on the change
result rather than offered behind a separate read. A `checked` advisory is a verdict the
emitter verified itself and needs no action; a warning is open, and its `instruction` is
the concrete check or edit that settles it. In a projection, an open warning also mints an
`advisory` confirmation, so publication cannot take the change until the caller accepts
it.

instruction.description: The concrete step that settles an open advisory: the check to run, or the edit to make. Null on a checked advisory.

Edit.description:
A filesystem effect described before Rift performs it. Edit sets are atomic and sorted
bytewise by each edit's RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

Text replacements in one set address the same input state and cannot overlap. An empty
range at `a` overlaps `[s, e)` only when `s < a < e`, so boundary insertions are legal; two
edits sharing an insertion point apply in the set's canonical order, and an insertion at
the start of a replacement lands before the replacement text.

Application runs in phases: text replacements against the pre-state, then deletes, copies,
renames, creates, and executable-bit changes. Structural sources read the pre-state, and
two structural edits contending for one path are `invalid_request` unless a delete freed
it.

ProjectPath.description:
One path below the workspace root, using forward slashes and UTF-8 in Unicode NFC — Rift
normalizes what it emits and what it accepts, and compares byte-for-byte. The empty path
names the root itself. Absolute paths, backslashes, control characters, empty segments, and
`.` or `..` segments are refused before the filesystem is touched. The limit is 1000 UTF-8
bytes, not characters. A workspace holding two entries whose NFC forms are equal fails the
read that touches them with `content_unavailable`.

Publishes one projection into the workspace. Publication settles change confirmations
and read-dependency conflicts because it is the step that writes into the workspace. The

accept.title: Accept

The result of publishing one projection's changes into the workspace. A successful
publication clears its changeset and recorded read dependencies; any listed conflict or

will vouch for still lands, carrying its confirmations — `ErrorData` carries

rift:enumDescriptions.ambiguous_target: The address resolves to several targets. Narrow it and ask again.
rift:enumDescriptions.unmet_precondition: A condition checked before resolution failed. The failed entry is in `preconditions`.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsafe_effect: The complete effect reaches outside what the caller can have meant — outside the project, or into generated source.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsupported: Nothing serves this operation for the language it reaches.

RegionRole.description: One named part of a node. A language marks these out inside a declaration, so an operation can address the body of a function without addressing its documentation.

rift:enumDescriptions.body: The implementation. Replacing it leaves the signature and the documentation standing.
rift:enumDescriptions.content: What the node holds where its interior is not code: the text of a comment, the characters inside a string.
rift:enumDescriptions.documentation: The doc comment for this declaration. In most languages it sits outside the declaration, which is why the node has to point at it.
rift:enumDescriptions.enclosing: The node with everything that belongs to it, documentation and annotations included. What a removal should take.
rift:enumDescriptions.header: Everything before the body — the keyword, the name, the parameters, the return type.
rift:enumDescriptions.name: The identifier alone.
rift:enumDescriptions.selection: What a caller should select on arriving here: the name for a declaration, the whole node otherwise.

Matching by portable facet, which reaches every served language.

facet.description: Portable relationship facets. Any listed facet matches.

target.description: What has to be true of the entity at the other end. Nesting a filter here is how "callers that are tests" becomes one query.

min_depth.description: How many edges to walk before a hit counts. Above 1 this asks about indirect neighbours and skips the direct ones.
min_depth.title: Min Depth

max_depth.description: How many edges a traversal may cross. Only edges that compose carry a depth — `contains`, `declares`, `augments`, `calls`, `imports`, `extends`, `implements`, `mixes_in`, `embeds`, `depends_on`. A bound above 1 on any other facet has nothing to walk, and Rift rejects it.
max_depth.title: Max Depth

quantifier.description: Whether a match needs such an edge, or needs there to be none.

RelationFilter.title: RelationFilter

RelationFilterDirection.description: Which way the edge runs, seen from the entity being filtered.

rift:enumDescriptions.incoming: Edges that point at it — its callers, its implementors.
rift:enumDescriptions.outgoing: Edges that start at the entity — what it calls, imports, extends.

RelationFilterDirection.title: RelationFilterDirection

RelationFilterQuantifier.description: Whether a match needs such an edge, or needs there to be none.

rift:enumDescriptions.not_exists: No edge matches. How "a symbol nothing calls" is written. It applies after the depth bound, so `max_depth: 3` asks about edges within three hops and says nothing about the fourth.

RelationFilterQuantifier.title: RelationFilterQuantifier

Relationship.description: One directed edge between two symbols. Its evidence is the nodes it was read from, and its derivation is how much the provider knew when it was read.

from.description: The symbol the edge starts at.

kind.description: What the edge is in this provider's vocabulary, such as `import`, `use`, or `implements`.

facets.description: Portable classification, so a query for `imports` finds local kinds such as `import` and `use` alike.
facets.title: Facets

to.description: The symbol the edge points at. One Rift cannot read carries the `external` origin; the edge is the same either way.

evidence.description: The nodes this edge was read from.
evidence.title: Evidence

confidence.description: How likely a `heuristic` edge is to hold, from 0 to 1. Absent for any other derivation.
confidence.title: Confidence

extensions.description: Edge facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted them.

Relationship.title: Relationship

RelationshipDerivation.description: How this edge was established. Every edge reaches Rift from a provider; this field records how much the provider knew. A consumer may act on `resolution` directly. Lower levels require another check before rewriting.

rift:enumDescriptions.heuristic: A guess, with `confidence` saying how good a one. Required there and meaningless elsewhere.
rift:enumDescriptions.resolution: The provider's own name resolution or type checker produced the edge. It is a fact about the program.
rift:enumDescriptions.syntax: Read off the syntax tree because nothing resolved it — a call on an untyped receiver matched by name. Repeatable, and still capable of being wrong.

RelationshipDerivation.title: RelationshipDerivation

RelationshipFacet.description: One portable category an edge falls into. The local kinds `import` and `use` can share the `imports` facet, which lets one query cross languages.

rift:enumDescriptions.aliases: `from` is another name for `to` — a type alias, a re-export, an `as` rename.
rift:enumDescriptions.annotated_by: `to` is attached to `from` as metadata: an annotation, a decorator, an attribute.
rift:enumDescriptions.augments: `from` adds members to `to`, which is declared elsewhere — a Rust `impl` block, a TypeScript `declare module`, an `ALTER TABLE`, a CSS rule for a selector another file already styles.
rift:enumDescriptions.binds: `from` names `to` across a language boundary: a `className` and the CSS rule it selects, an ORM entity and its table.
rift:enumDescriptions.bounded_by: `from` is constrained to satisfy `to` — the `Serialize` in `T: Serialize`, the `Comparable` in `<T extends Comparable<T>>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.catches: `from` handles `to` when something it calls raises it.
rift:enumDescriptions.configures: `from` supplies configuration `to` reads — a `rift.toml` key and the field it fills, a `tsconfig` path alias and the module it resolves.
rift:enumDescriptions.contains: `from` lexically holds `to` — a module and the functions written in it.
rift:enumDescriptions.declares: `from` owns `to`. A class carries this to its methods even where the language writes them outside its body.
rift:enumDescriptions.depends_on: `from` needs `to` and there is no place in the source to point at — a manifest entry or build dependency.
rift:enumDescriptions.embeds: `from` holds `to` and promotes its members, so they are reachable without naming the field. Go struct embedding.
rift:enumDescriptions.generates: `to` was produced from `from` by a build step, so editing `to` lasts until the next build.
rift:enumDescriptions.has_type: `to` is the type of `from`. What jump-to-type-definition follows.
rift:enumDescriptions.imports: `from` brings `to` in from another unit. A header or a stylesheet that declares nothing of its own is a synthetic `module` symbol, so `#include` and `@import` are the same edge as a Python `import`.
rift:enumDescriptions.instantiates: `from` applies `to` as a type argument — the `Config` in `Vec<Config>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.mixes_in: `from` takes members from `to` by linearization — a Dart `with` clause, a Scala mixin. The order they are written in decides which one wins.
rift:enumDescriptions.overloads: `from` and `to` share a name and differ in signature, and the language picks between them at the call site.
rift:enumDescriptions.reads: `from` takes the value of `to`. A SQL `SELECT` against a table is this edge.
rift:enumDescriptions.references: `from` mentions `to` somewhere in the source and nothing narrower fits. The fallback edge where there is a node to point at.
rift:enumDescriptions.specializes: `from` is a narrower form of `to`, chosen over it where both match.
rift:enumDescriptions.tests: `from` exercises `to`. A test that reaches its target through reflection or HTTP has no call edge to carry it.
rift:enumDescriptions.writes: `from` assigns to `to`. A SQL `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is this edge.

RelationshipFacet.title: RelationshipFacet

SearchParams.description: Criteria for one search. The caller supplies at least one of lexical `query`, provider `filter`, or relationship `traversal`; `scope` selects source locations, and `paths` narrows project-only searches.

target.description: Which entity kinds may be returned — a kind selector, never the text to search for; that is `query`. Omitted, every kind may match. Type data is attached to the Symbol and Node records that bind it, and filters can search those attachments.

order.description: Which total order the page comes back in. The cursor is bound to it, so it cannot change between pages of one query. Omitted, relevance.

query.description: Text to match against file contents, symbol names, and rendered signatures. filter.description: A predicate over resolved fields and relationships. This is where provider knowledge enters a search — implements this trait, called by that function, declared under `src/api`.

paths.description: Files eligible for the search, selected by project-relative globs. Omitted selects every visible file.

include.description: Extra payload to attach to every hit. Each entry costs a lookup per hit, so the caller requests only what it will read.

limit.description: Most hits to return in one page. `max_page_items` from the workspace resource caps it, and fewer may come back.

projection.description: The projection to search. Null searches the workspace tree.

traversal.description: A bounded relationship walk. It may stand alone or add graph hits to a lexical or filtered search; duplicate symbols keep their shortest path.

scope.description: Source locations eligible for results. Project is the default; select dependencies or all when the answer may live outside the workspace.

rift:enumDescriptions.all: Every kind above, in one ranked list.

rift:enumDescriptions.node: Places in a syntax tree where a symbol is written. One symbol has many.
rift:enumDescriptions.symbol: Declarations a provider resolved — a function, a class, a trait.

intent.description: The task whose defaults rank and narrow the walk. `find_tests` returns test symbols; other intents return every eligible symbol.

direction.description: Direction to walk. Omitted selects incoming for `find_tests` and `edit_ripple`, outgoing for `trace`, and both for `review_context`.

facets.description: Portable relationship facets eligible for expansion. Omitted selects `tests` for `find_tests` and `calls` for every other intent; an empty list is `invalid_request`.
facets.title: Facets

max_hops.description: Maximum path length from `seed`. The server accepts 1 or 2; one hop is the default because a second hop can multiply weak edges.
max_hops.title: Max Hops

max_nodes.description: Most distinct graph symbols the server may visit, excluding `seed`. Filtering can make the answer shorter than this bound.

ServerLock.description:
The rendezvous record at `.rift/server.json`, written by the server that owns the
workspace and read by every process that wants to reach it. Atomic creation of the file
is the election: the process that creates it starts the server, and everyone else
connects to the endpoint it names. The file is readable by its owner alone, so holding
the token is what authorizes a connection — localhost TCP carries no peer identity the
server could check instead.

port.description: TCP port on `127.0.0.1` where the server accepts HTTP.
port.title: Port

pid.description: Process id of the owning server, for staleness checks. A reader that cannot reach the endpoint verifies the process before removing the file and re-running the election.
pid.title: Pid

token.description: Bearer token every HTTP request carries in `Authorization`. The server refuses a request without it.
token.title: Token

workspace.description: Canonical absolute path of the workspace the server serves.

rift:enumDescriptions.error: Code the provider would not accept. Facts read from around it may be missing.
rift:enumDescriptions.info: Something worth knowing that is not a defect.
rift:enumDescriptions.warning: Code that parses and the provider judges wrong anyway.

Symbol.description: Provider-resolved semantic identity. Source structure lives in Node and is connected through Relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier of this symbol across the whole workspace, and the URI that change requests, filters, and relationship records accept unchanged.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

name.description: The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered signatures live in `signatures`.
name.title: Name

kind.description: What this symbol is in the provider's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or `table`.

facets.description: Portable classification for cross-language queries. The local kinds `trait` and `interface` can both carry the `type` facet.
facets.title: Facets

origin.description: Where the declaration belongs, how it was produced, and its source unit when readable.

container.description: The symbol this one belongs to — the class that owns a method, the module that owns a function. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type and a Rust method inside an `impl` block, and both name the type here. Absent at the top level.

visibility.description: How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms — `public`, `private`, `pub(crate)`. Null where the language has no such concept.
visibility.title: Visibility

types.description: The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a field type, a bound.
types.title: Types

signatures.description: One entry per callable form. Where the language dispatches overloads separately they are separate symbols joined by the `overloads` edge; several entries here are alternative forms of one dispatch target, as `typing.overload` writes them.
signatures.title: Signatures

documentation.description: Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written in.
documentation.title: Documentation

extensions.description: Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the provider that emitted them.

document_local.description: Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The provider classifies locality from its language model.
document_local.title: Document Local

Symbol.title: Symbol

SymbolFacet.description: One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are shared, so a filter written once applies to every served language.

rift:enumDescriptions.abstract: Declared without an implementation. Whatever carries `implements` or `extends` to it has to supply one.
rift:enumDescriptions.alias: Another name for a symbol declared elsewhere — a `typealias`, a C++ `using`, a re-export. The `aliases` edge says which symbol.
rift:enumDescriptions.annotation: Declared to be attached to another declaration: a Java `@interface`, a Kotlin `annotation class`, a Python decorator, a Rust attribute macro.
rift:enumDescriptions.async: Produces a value that completes later. `Signature.effects` keeps the language's own keyword: `async`, `suspend`.
rift:enumDescriptions.callable: Can be called, and so carries at least one `Signature`.
rift:enumDescriptions.constructor: The callable that produces an instance. `constructible` marks the type it produces.
rift:enumDescriptions.deprecated: Marked as no longer to be used, however the language spells it — `@Deprecated`, `#[deprecated]`, a doc tag.
rift:enumDescriptions.entrypoint: Where execution starts: `fn main`, `func main`, a `bin` script named by the package manifest.
rift:enumDescriptions.enumeration: Declares the closed set those variants belong to. A `match` over it is exhaustive once every variant is covered.
rift:enumDescriptions.extensible: Can be inherited from or overridden: a non-`final` class, a Kotlin `open fun`, a C++ `virtual` method.
rift:enumDescriptions.extension: Attached to a type declared somewhere else — a Kotlin extension function, a method in a Rust `impl` block, a Go method, a Dart extension.
rift:enumDescriptions.generator: Yields a sequence one value at a time instead of returning once — a Python generator, a Dart `sync*` function.
rift:enumDescriptions.implementable: Names a contract another type can satisfy: an interface, a trait, a protocol.
rift:enumDescriptions.macro: Expands source at compile time, as `macro_rules!` and preprocessor definitions do.
rift:enumDescriptions.member: Owned by another symbol — a method, a field, an enum variant. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type, and a Rust method inside an `impl` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.member_container: Can hold members: a class, a struct, an interface.
rift:enumDescriptions.module: A unit the language imports whole. A TypeScript file carries this facet, and so do a Rust `mod` and a Go package, both of which can span several files.
rift:enumDescriptions.mutable: Can be reassigned after it is initialized. A Rust `let mut` carries it, a `let` does not.
rift:enumDescriptions.namespace: Groups names without being a unit the language loads — a C++ `namespace`, a Java package, a SQL schema.
rift:enumDescriptions.operator: Invoked through operator syntax — C++ `operator+`, Python `__add__`, a Kotlin `operator fun`.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: A parameter of a callable, declared as a symbol of its own so it can be renamed and referred to.
rift:enumDescriptions.property: Read and written as a value, and backed by code that runs — a Kotlin property, a Python `@property`, a JavaScript getter.
rift:enumDescriptions.public: Reachable from outside the unit that declares it. `visibility` carries the language's own word, which Go and Python do not have: there the provider reads the naming convention.
rift:enumDescriptions.static: Bound to the declaration rather than to an instance, so a call needs no receiver.
rift:enumDescriptions.test: The language's test tooling collects it as a test: a `#[test]` function, a `describe` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.type: Declares a type. `struct Config` and `interface Props` both qualify, which is what makes one search for types find both.
rift:enumDescriptions.type_parameter: A generic parameter — the `T` in `Vec<T>`. A Rust lifetime and a C++ `template<int N>` carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.value: Names something that exists while the program runs: a variable, a constant, a function object. A CSS class selector and a SQL sequence carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.variant: One case of a closed set: a Rust enum variant, a Scala `case`, a Java enum constant.

SymbolHistory.description: One symbol's timeline across the workspace's version-control history, newest revision first. The walk is bounded by the configured history depth, so `coverage` says whether the timeline reaches the symbol's introduction.

symbol.description: The symbol the timeline is for.

versions.description: Revisions that touched the symbol, newest first.
versions.title: Versions

coverage.description: How far back the walk reached. Partial means the configured depth ended before the symbol's introduction, so an absent `introduced` version proves nothing.

SymbolId.description:
Identity of one symbol. The name after the language is the provider's stable qualified
name for the declaration; where the language derives module identity from the file path,
as TypeScript does, that path is part of the name. A `~N` suffix separates declarations
the qualified name alone cannot, such as overloads that dispatch separately. A move can
change the identity when the language includes module path in that qualified name; history
correlation records the declaration across that change.

SymbolOrigin.description:
Where a symbol belongs and how its declaration came to exist. Source location and
generation are separate: generated code can belong to the project or to a dependency.

location.description: Source ownership. Null exactly when `source_kind` is `synthetic`.

source_kind.description: Whether the declaration is authored, generated, or synthetic.

unit.description: Source-catalog unit containing the declaration. Null when source is unavailable or the declaration is synthetic.

SymbolOrigin.title: SymbolOrigin

SymbolVersion.description: One revision that touched a symbol. The history provider derives it by parsing the declaration at each revision that changed its file, so a version exists only where the parse found the symbol.

revision.description: The revision that touched the symbol.

path.description: Where the declaration lived at that revision.

timestamp.description: When the revision was recorded, as RFC 3339 date-time.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

summary.description: The revision's own first summary line, where the version control records one.
summary.title: Summary

SymbolVersion.title: SymbolVersion

SymbolVersionKind.description: What the revision did to the symbol.

rift:enumDescriptions.body_changed: The implementation changed while the header stayed.
rift:enumDescriptions.decorators_changed: The declaration's attached decorators changed while the header and body stayed. Behavior may change without either.
rift:enumDescriptions.introduced: The revision that first declares the symbol.
rift:enumDescriptions.moved: The history provider matched the declaration across a file move; `path` records where it lives at this revision.
rift:enumDescriptions.removed: The declaration is gone after this revision.
rift:enumDescriptions.signature_changed: The header changed, so every caller written before this revision predates the current shape.
